proposed_widenings.name: ReactionTrigger.spell_targets_only_self_no_area
proposed_widenings.justification: The current reaction trigger grammar cannot express a reaction to any spell that targets only the wielder and has no area of effect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While holding this rod, you can take a Reaction to absorb a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect.

proposed_widenings.name: absorbed_spell_energy_reservoir
proposed_widenings.justification: The item needs a persistent reservoir that gains variable energy from absorbed spell levels, enforces a lifetime absorption ceiling of 50, and can stop absorbing permanently once that ceiling is reached.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and the spell's energy-not the spell itself-is stored in the rod. The energy has the same level as the spell when it was cast. The rod can absorb and store up to 50 levels of energy over the course of its existence.

proposed_widenings.name: spell_slot_substitution_from_item_energy
proposed_widenings.justification: The rod does not grant named spells. It lets a spellcaster spend stored item energy as spell-slot levels to cast their own prepared or known spells, with level limits derived from the wielder.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you are a spellcaster holding the rod, you can convert energy stored in it into spell slots to cast spells you have prepared or know. You can create spell slots only of a level equal to or lower than your own spell slots, up to a maximum of level 5.

proposed_widenings.name: ItemDestructionPolicy.becomes_nonmagical_when_depleted_after_lifetime_cap
proposed_widenings.justification: Existing destruction policies do not model an item that permanently stops absorbing at a lifetime threshold and later becomes nonmagical only once its remaining stored energy is also exhausted.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A rod that can no longer absorb spell energy and has no energy remaining becomes nonmagical.

notes: Top-level kind and composite magic-item family exist, but the current surface cannot honestly encode the generic spell-absorption trigger, the absorbed-energy reservoir, or the slot-substitution mechanic. No content or trace file was produced.
